newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier as options expiry.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier as options expiry.

text.p: Precious metals prices turned easier on Tuesday afternoon following a lower opening in New York and uneventful expiry of over the counter (OTC) options.
"The options didn't make much difference but the buy-back (from Newmont Mining) helped and volatilities are a bit higher," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $326.55 per ounce down from $327.50 at the morning fix. On Monday gold fixed at $325.75.
In New York the Comex December contract was down $2.40 at $331.00 having taken over as the most active contract as August approached its notice period.
Dealers said gold had run into stiff opposition at over $328.00 from profit taking and producers selling into the relatively higher price.
The extent of short covering involved in Monday's rise was witnessed by a fall in implied lease rates from over 200 basis points to 181 basis points this morning.
"The forward market is telling us the price wants to go higher," a dealer said. But he added, "The producers are still lining up to sell."
The North American producer Newmont Mining late on Monday announced it had bought back 1.1 million ounces of hedged gold to lock in $90 per ounce above the cash price.
Last week South Africa's Western Areas announced it had bought 1.6 million ounces of gold in the market to give it upside price exposure.
In 1995 it had hedged 7.3 million ounces of gold and bought call options on four million ounces of metal.
Technical analysts said gold had to get through the $329-$330 area where it has now failed four times in order to reach the seven month downtrend at $335.70.
"If it gets through the breakout point I expect it to get to $335.70 but not higher," one technician said.
The white metals also stepped back this afternoon with silver edging a few cents lower with gold to $4.36/$4.38 having looked as though it might make another attempt to move higher.
Platinum and palladium were both off Monday's highs reflecting some dealer profit taking.
Some dealers said Russia had been offering material in the European dealer market but had not found many buyers.
Platinum was down $3.50 at $426.00/$429.00 and palladium was $3.00 lower at $202.00/$204.00
